entities.label: Jesus’ ministry

scholarly.note: Chronology of the public ministry varies by a few years; region cues matter more than exact dates.

entities.traditionalNote: Public ministry centered in Galilee with journeys to Judea and Jerusalem.

entities.label: Acts

scholarly.note: Narrative ends with Paul in Rome; composition is often placed decades after the earliest events.

entities.traditionalNote: From Jerusalem witness to Paul’s missions across the Roman world.

entities.label: Galatians

scholarly.note: Widely accepted as Pauline; exact year depends on North/South Galatia theories.

entities.traditionalNote: Paul’s letter on gospel and covenant to churches in Galatia.

entities.label: 1 Thessalonians

scholarly.note: Among Paul’s earliest surviving letters; strong scholarly consensus on authenticity.

entities.traditionalNote: Early Pauline encouragement to a young Macedonian congregation.

entities.label: 1 Corinthians

scholarly.note: Undisputed Paul; written from Ephesus to a fractious Corinthian church.

entities.traditionalNote: Pastoral letter addressing division, worship, and resurrection hope.

entities.label: 2 Corinthians

scholarly.note: Pauline; some see it as combining more than one letter fragment.

entities.traditionalNote: Paul defends his apostleship and reconciles with Corinth.

entities.label: Romans

scholarly.note: Undisputed Paul; usually placed near the end of the Aegean mission period.

entities.traditionalNote: Paul’s sustained presentation of the gospel to the Roman churches.

entities.label: Philippians

scholarly.note: Accepted as Pauline; scholars debate whether from Rome, Ephesus, or Caesarea.

entities.traditionalNote: Joyful letter from custody to a supportive Macedonian church.

scholarly.note: Undisputed Paul; closely tied to the Onesimus situation and often to Colossians.

entities.label: Colossians

scholarly.note: Some attribute to Paul in custody; others see a later Pauline school.

entities.traditionalNote: Christ-centered letter to a church Paul may not have visited.

entities.label: Ephesians

scholarly.note: Many scholars see a circular Pauline-tradition letter rather than a situation-specific note from Paul.

entities.traditionalNote: Broad teaching on church unity and life in Christ.

entities.label: 2 Thessalonians

scholarly.note: Some accept Pauline authorship soon after 1 Thessalonians; others argue for a later hand.

entities.traditionalNote: Follow-up on endurance and the day of the Lord.

entities.label: Pastoral Epistles

scholarly.note: 1–2 Timothy and Titus are frequently dated after Paul’s death as church-order letters in his name.

entities.traditionalNote: 1–2 Timothy and Titus on leadership and sound teaching.

entities.label: Hebrews

scholarly.dateLabel: Author unknown; often pre- or post-70
scholarly.note: Not Pauline in most modern critical views; a sophisticated sermon on Christ’s priesthood.

entities.traditionalNote: Anonymous sermon-letter exalting Christ over earlier covenants.

entities.label: James

scholarly.note: Some see very early Jewish-Christian wisdom; others a later circular letter.

entities.traditionalNote: Practical wisdom on faith lived out.

entities.label: 1 Peter

scholarly.note: Traditional Petrine authorship is debated; addresses believers under social pressure in Asia Minor.

entities.traditionalNote: Hope and holiness for Christians facing hostility.

entities.label: 1 John

scholarly.note: Usually linked to Johannine circles in Asia Minor rather than a simple private note from the apostle.

entities.traditionalNote: Tests of discipleship: truth, love, and confession of Christ.

entities.label: Revelation

scholarly.note: Apocalypse to Asian churches; majority prefer a late-1st-century Roman setting.

entities.traditionalNote: Visions of judgment and hope under imperial pressure.
